processing_steps.method: melting and casting in a vacuum-induction melting (VIM) furnace
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: System modified to synthesize five different alloys in one operation per alloy system, using five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace; melts cast from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10×50×130 mm³ blocks were hot rolled into 2±0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
After reheating and water quenching, sheets were cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into nine segments of 2×60×55 mm³ per alloy composition.
Aging was conducted in air at 450, 500, 550 and 600 °C for 0 h, 1 h and 24 h at each temperature, followed by oil quenching; this sample is the 600 °C, 1 h condition.
Scales were removed from the surfaces after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized austenitic (fcc) microstructure with a grain size of ~20 µm and some retained Mn microsegregations; Al-free single-phase austenite

defects.type: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations detected

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

hardness.uncertainty: aging increases hardness slightly relative to the as-homogenized state

characterization_methods.purpose: Hardness screening as a function of Al content and aging condition
characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness nearly flat ~200 HBW from 0Al to 6Al for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl set.

characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; hot rolling and water quenching gave a fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 µm grain size and retained Mn microsegregations.

unmapped_findings: For the Al-free reference alloy Fe-30Mn-1.2C (0 wt.% Al), the best mechanical behavior is in the as-homogenized state: 360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS (high work hardening), and 77% TE. Aging leaves the YS virtually unchanged and slightly increases the hardness, but reduces UTS and TE. (The 360/830/77 values belong to the as-homogenized parent condition, not to the 600 °C/1 h aged sample; no exact numeric YS/UTS/TE values are reported in the text for the 600 °C/1 h aged condition of this alloy.)

Embrittlement of the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy becomes most apparent for long aging times (24 h) and higher temperatures (>500 °C); the 600 °C/1 h condition is a high-temperature but short-time aging treatment.

In the RAP screening plots (Fig. 3), the 0Al Fe-30Mn-1.2C composition shows YS between roughly the 350 and 450 MPa lines (all aging conditions), UTS highest for the as-homogenised condition (above 800 MPa), TE highest for as-homogenised (~80%), and hardness nearly flat at ~200 HBW from 0Al to 6Al; the 600 °C/1 h (olive) curve lies within these bands at 0Al.

In the tensile strength vs elongation plot (Fig. 4), the Al-free (0Al) Fe-30Mn-1.2C series follows the 'T + t' trend from about 490 MPa at ~8% elongation to about 800 MPa at ~70% elongation (annotation T: 1 h; T+t: 24 h).

κ-carbides (L′1₂, approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)₃AlC) require Al and form upon aging in Al-containing variants; the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C sample is not expected to contain κ-carbides, consistent with its single-phase austenite (SIMPLEX/TWIP) behavior.

The Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl set was screened as a matrix of 45 different sample conditions (five Al levels × nine heat treatments), giving 135 tensile tests and hardness measurements for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C base composition.
